scenarios.when: GET https://api.puretokensx.com/v1 returns status ok, name Pure Tokens API, and base_url /v1
scenarios.then: State only that the fixed API returns the expected public identity. This does not verify credentials, funds, model authorization or media/attachment availability.

scenarios.when: A command for the bound host returns an active_connection_*, workbuddy_*, or host_credential_adapter_unavailable local failure, including when the user asks to continue generation.
scenarios.then: Stop the automatic API flow. Do not invoke connection, init, doctor, models, another Skill, or another --host as a recovery probe. Preserve the original request and any existing task ID; never resubmit automatically. Explain only that this invocation sent no API request. An explicit recheck request or verified new diagnostic evidence permits one relevant check on the same host; changing host requires explicit user selection.

scenarios.when: GET https://api.puretokensx.com/v1 returns unreadable JSON, missing fields, or values other than the declared Pure Tokens API identity
scenarios.then: state that the fixed Pure Tokens API did not return a confirmable identity and do not assert that the user's other connection belongs to another service

scenarios.when: the direct GET https://api.puretokensx.com/v1 request fails
scenarios.then: state that the fixed API could not be checked, report the returned result when available, and do not try another endpoint or request credentials

scenarios.when: the user explicitly asks to verify the fixed API public identity and the managed native executor can run
scenarios.then: invoke the installed managed native executor with the current host ID for the fixed identity GET; do not look for a separate connection interface

scenarios.when: the user asks for their actual configured Base URL, API key, provider label, or host configuration
scenarios.then: state that only the native executor may use the matching documented connection credential in memory only to make the fixed request, but never displays, compares, or reports host configuration; direct the user to their client or CC Switch settings and clarify that media Skills themselves use the fixed Pure Tokens API origin

scenarios.when: the user needs proof stronger than the API endpoint public identity declaration
scenarios.then: explain that the existing check validates the endpoint declaration only and does not claim cryptographic anti-spoof verification

scenarios.when: the user asks what Pure Tokens is, what it does or how to get started, without requesting public API identity verification
scenarios.then: Use puretokens-update local usage guidance without a connection request, executor call, host question, credential read or network access. A general current-connection/authentication check uses init once, not this identity-only operation.
